title: Autonomous Rollout Sheriff and Traffic Attenuation Policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an autonomous ‘Rollout Sheriff’ service that continuously evaluates canary and ramping releases against safety predicates and applies attenuation actions (pause, throttle, divert, rollback) automatically. This work ties together versioning/LTS channels, rollout gates, and upgrade tooling so that we can safely automate fast rollouts with predictable failure modes and clear audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Sheriff evaluates a configured rollout (version + channel + traffic plan) and emits decisions at each ramp step within 30s of metric ingestion

Support at least three attenuation actions: PAUSE (halt traffic increase), THROTTLE (reduce target ramp rate), DIVERT (route failing cohorts to previous stable version), ROLLBACK (promote stable version and remove new version)
Config-driven safety predicates: error rate, P95 latency, token-level cost delta, user-visible degradations; thresholds are per-project and per-channel
Integrates with feature flag system to gate code paths and to coordinate partial user cohorts
All automated decisions are logged with causal links to traces/dashboards and surfaced in Console with an explainer and ‘replay’ button
Manual override path that honors 'hold' and 'force-rollout' ops flags with RBAC checks
End-to-end tests (integration + canary simulation) exercising both healthy and failure ramps are in CI with deterministic assertion hooks
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff — aligned with PM and SRE on primary metrics (error_rate_5m, p95_latency, auth_fail_rate). Chose candidate metric names and ingestion paths.
2026-03-04: Design review with Console team — decided to surface Sheriff decisions in new 'Rollouts' tab (Console-PRD link added). Need UI mockups for explainer and action buttons.

2026-03-06: Prototype of decision engine implemented (stateless evaluation) — supports threshold and rolling-window comparison against baseline. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sheriff/tree/prototype
2026-03-08: SRE feedback: require backoff/retry when metric ingestion latency spikes; added jitter to ramp timers to avoid blast radius from synchronized ramps

2026-03-10: Implemented DIVERT action via router-change API; integration test for divert to fallback version passes in staging. Follow-up: add audit+trace link in router change PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/482)
notes: Tradeoffs: we prefer automated attenuation for low-severity SLO breaches but keep manual escalation for high-severity incidents. Using an additive scoring model for multiple small signals rather than thresholding a single metric to reduce noisy rollbacks. Key open question: exact scoring weights per-product — default weights will be conservative and product teams can tune per-project.
testing_plan: Unit tests for the decision evaluator; deterministic canary simulator that replays historical traffic patterns; chaos runbook to verify safe rollback under router failure. CI gates will block merges until simulator tests pass.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: shadow-mode across 5% of traffic for internal customers; Phase 2: supervised automation on beta channel (traffic ramps controlled by Sheriff but require PM ack to advance); Phase 3: fully autonomous on non-LTS channels with configurable safety-strictness. LTS channels default to manual approvals and strict thresholds.
postmortem_plan: If an automated attenuation results in significant customer impact, trigger immediate rollback to stable and create PM+SRE postmortem. Sheriff will capture decision timeline and metrics snapshot to bootstrap postmortem.
